02 · The problem

Trade finance today

A lender sees paperwork, not the container.

So it lends blind, or does not lend at all. The exporter waits about two months for cash it has already earned, while the cargo is at risk in transit.

Daniel, the financier, holds the documents. The reefer stays out of sight.

Atradius Payment Practices Barometer India 2025: average B2B payment terms of 52 days

05 · The solution

The solution

Capital that answers to the cargo's evidence.

1

A financier escrows USDG for one shipment.

2

Tranches release only when signed sensor evidence passes an on-chain policy.

3

The buyer's one payment repays the financier, pays the exporter and hands over the bill of lading.

Illustrative characters. Everything they do is a real contract call.

06 · How it works

How it works

Five steps, every one on chain.

1

Escrow

Daniel deposits the 40,000 USDG facility into the vault.

2

Evidence

Signed readings fuse into a score from 0 to 100.

3

Release

Evidence passes the policy: 8,000 USDG to Meera.

4

Pause, prove

Score 48 pauses it; a Groth16 proof resumes it.

5

Settle

One 100,000 USDG payment splits and moves the title.

Reference numbers: 100,000 USDG invoice, 40,000 USDG facility, 3% fee.

createFacility · depositCapital · commitEpoch · evaluateAndReleaseMilestone · pauseFinancing · resumeWithProof · settle (contracts v3, 3 Oct 2026)

06 / 21

07 · Safety nets

Built into the contracts

Safety nets are part of the protocol.

Title moves with money

The carrier's ERC-721 bill of lading leaves escrow inside the buyer's payment.

Automatic recovery

A proof is prepared once a probe has eight fresh in-band readings. The exporter signs once.

Parametric cover

Pays out after N failed epochs in a row, proven from the commit order.

Disputes go to an arbiter role that can never release money · README "Under the hood" · docs/architecture.md

11 · Technology and moat

Technology and moat

Five mechanisms that enforce each other.

01

Signed readings

Each device signs; every epoch records its source.

02

Fusion score

Dempster-Shafer fusion with a published formula.

03

Bound ZK proof

Groth16, bound to the contract's own signals.

04

Locked vault

Only the controller's rules release USDG.

05

Title with payment

The bill of lading moves inside the payment.

A copy needs all five, tested together: 366 contract tests and 25 circuit tests.

Groth16: 13,494 constraints, about 1 s to prove, about 0.25 M gas to verify · immutable core, eight fuzzed invariants · docs/architecture.md, docs/benchmarks.md

15 · Business model

Business model

Paid when capital moves, not before.

01

Protocol fee

30 to 50 bps of each drawn facility, inside the settlement waterfall (A3).

02

Cover premiums

A share of default and parametric cover written through the CoverPool.

03

Software and data

Portfolio risk, evidence API and MCP for funds and insurers.

One 100,000 USDG payment, split on chain (reference facility)

58,800 to the exporter

40,000 principal

1,200

Principal and the 3% fee go to the financier. The protocol fee is one more line in this split.

Non-custodial: the ReceivableVault is the sole USDG custodian · fee levels are planned (A3) · contracts/src/ReceivableVault.sol, CoverPool.sol, packages/python
